description: Fictional English incident handoff with corrected measurements, rejected remedies, named speaker responsibilities and a provisional test decision.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Before I hand over, let's separate facts from guesses. The slow exports occurred in the test environment this morning. We haven't seen the same failure in production.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Understood. The dashboard shows three failures out of forty attempts. Were those all requests from the same test account?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: They used the same account and report template. That narrows the investigation, but it doesn't prove the account caused the problem or that every template is affected.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Someone suggested restarting every worker before the next test. Should I do that as soon as the handover is finished?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: No, leave the workers running. A restart could erase useful evidence. First capture the queue length, worker logs, and request identifiers from the affected interval.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I've checked the dashboard again. I misread one column. There were four failed attempts out of forty, and the warning threshold was twenty five seconds, not twenty.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thanks. I'll put four failures and twenty five seconds in the note. Let's remove the earlier figures so nobody quotes both sets as though they describe separate tests.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The retry limit is currently two. Would raising it to five give the export enough time to finish without changing anything else?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We aren't approving that change. Extra retries could lengthen the queue and hide the original delay. Keep the limit at two, and don't disable the timeout warning.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: All right. What will you collect before you leave, and which follow up should I own during the next shift?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I'll export the logs and request identifiers by two this afternoon, including the time zone and test template version. Matching timestamps without those details could send us in the wrong direction.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll prepare the rollback checklist. Is tomorrow at eleven in the morning early enough, or do you need a draft today?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Tomorrow at eleven is fine. Cover the settings and worker version separately. The checklist should explain how to reverse a change, without implying a rollback has already been approved.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Should I tell the test team that Friday's larger run can proceed? They asked whether they could start booking the machines now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Friday is provisional. We'll review the evidence on Thursday at ten, then decide whether to confirm the larger run. We can't promise approval before we understand the repeated failures.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I'll mark the booking as tentative. If another export fails during my shift, I'll add its identifier instead of opening an unrelated incident.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. Record successful attempts too. Comparing only failures could make a normal delay look unusual, and we'd lose evidence that might distinguish the two.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One last question. Have we established whether the delay starts in the network or after the request reaches the worker?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Not yet. That's the open question. I'll post the logs today, you'll deliver the checklist tomorrow, and we'll decide what happens next at Thursday's review.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: That's clear. Four failures out of forty, a twenty five second warning, two retries, and no restart or larger run approved yet.
